sections.title: JAX-Nano: A GPU-Accelerated Differentiable Phonon Boltzmann Transport Solver for Nanoscale Heat Transfer
sections.abstract: The authors introduce a GPU-accelerated, differentiable finite-volume solver for steady and transient phonon Boltzmann transport, validated across transport regimes and applied to 3D FinFETs and inverse parameter identification.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report agreement with analytical and established BTE solvers across diffusive-to-ballistic regimes, and demonstrate automatic-differentiation-based recovery of transport and heat-source parameters.
sections.evidence_type: computational; numerical benchmarks, analytical solutions, established BTE solvers, and simulated FinFET configurations
sections.unique_caveat: This is a numerical framework rather than experimental validation of device temperatures; its benchmark speed depends on hardware and workload. The authors identify fuller phonon dispersion/scattering models and memory efficiency as future work.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 1.00, entirely from 4 cross-lists (weighted component 1.00); highest score in the pool. No external-attention component is recorded.

sections.title: Validating Gaia DR3 Astrometric Accelerations with Close Visual Binaries
sections.abstract: The authors compare Gaia DR3 acceleration solutions with the gravitational effects and sky directions of known resolved visual-binary companions, finding consistency for a selected subset and identifying likely unresolved perturbers in most cross-matches.
sections.claimed_result: From 2,466 Gaia–Washington Double Star pairs, the authors find 98.1% of measured accelerations exceed the maximum attributable acceleration from the listed companion by more than a factor of ten; of 13 plausible systems with enough data for a test, 11 statistically accommodate the reported accelerations.
sections.evidence_type: observational; Gaia DR3 and Washington Double Star catalog cross-match, companion-orbit fits, and a direction test
sections.unique_caveat: This validates a catalog-matched subset, not all Gaia acceleration solutions. Many plausible pairs lack sufficient resolved astrometry for fitting, and the authors discuss WDS resolution and companion-mass uncertainties.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.75, entirely from 3 cross-lists (weighted component 0.75); tied at this score with several candidates. The physical cross-check and submitted-to-AJ comment support its selection among ties; no external-attention component is recorded.

sections.title: Time-variable tertiary mass transfer in hierarchical triple systems
sections.abstract: Three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations show that the inner binary’s finite separation can change a tertiary donor’s mass-loss variability and mean transfer rate, with implications for whether transferred gas forms a circumbinary disk.
sections.claimed_result: For the modeled γ=5/3 polytropic donor, the authors find a steep, approximately a_b^(6.1±0.9)-dependent rise in orbit-averaged mass loss as inner-binary separation increases, and a transition between individual and collaborative accretion.
sections.evidence_type: computational; three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations of a hierarchical triple configuration
sections.unique_caveat: The reported scaling is tied to the modeled donor and system assumptions, including equal-mass inner-binary components; grid mapping of the hydrostatic stellar profile is resolution-sensitive and computationally costly.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.75 from 3 cross-lists (weighted component 0.75). Its 3D simulations address an explicitly poorly understood phase of triple-star evolution; no external-attention component is recorded.

sections.title: A high-speed and high-resolution 3D velocity map imaging system with a neuromorphic camera
sections.abstract: The authors demonstrate a camera-based 3D velocity-map imaging system using an event-driven neuromorphic camera to detect single ions or electrons with microsecond latency.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report 2 μs single-particle detection latency and momentum-imaging operation above 100 kHz, compared with a few kHz for their conventional frame-camera reference.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; event-driven camera coupled to a microchannel-plate imaging detector
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract establishes a prototype demonstration but does not provide a broad uncertainty budget or performance comparison across other imaging platforms.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.75 from 3 cross-lists (weighted component 0.75); its detector-method cross-listing spans instrumentation, computer vision, nuclear experiment, and chemical physics. No external-attention component is recorded.

sections.title: The Thue-Morse route to chaos in the open quantum baker map
sections.abstract: Numerical resonance spectra of an open quantum baker map track a Thue–Morse sequence of classical survivor cycles as the opening crosses from zero to positive topological entropy.
sections.claimed_result: The author reports that numerically computed resonances follow the classical Thue–Morse route step by step up to Hilbert-space dimension N=2^25, including the zero-entropy regime.
sections.evidence_type: computational; classical-map analysis and numerical diagonalization/Arnoldi calculations of open quantum-map resonances
sections.unique_caveat: At the largest sizes only about four cycle steps are resolved. The paper leaves the asymptotic behavior of the leading resonance and the Fourier-basis fractal-Weyl exponent open.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.75 from 3 cross-lists (weighted component 0.75); it connects nonlinear dynamics, mathematical physics, and quantum physics and includes ancillary verification scripts. No external-attention component is recorded.

sections.title: An all-orders proof of gradient flow for multiscalar φ⁴ theory in four dimensions
sections.abstract: The author proves that the perturbative renormalization-group flow of four-dimensional multiscalar φ⁴ theory is a gradient flow to all orders, with a positive-definite metric.
sections.claimed_result: The author derives a symmetric positive metric and potential for the flow using Weyl consistency conditions and a Ward identity, and checks the implied five-/six-loop coefficient relations explicitly.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; perturbative quantum field theory and explicit loop-coefficient calculations
sections.unique_caveat: The proof is conditional on stated perturbative assumptions, including finiteness of the generating functional with local couplings and a bounded remainder for the large-momentum Feynman-integral expansion; it is not a nonperturbative result.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.75 from 3 cross-lists (weighted component 0.75), placing it among the most cross-listed candidates; its explicit all-orders result and check of five-/six-loop relations distinguish it among ties. No external-attention component is recorded.

sections.title: Observation of nonadiabatic quantum tunneling in a driven correlated insulator
sections.abstract: Time-resolved optical spectroscopy of NiPS₃ finds ponderomotively blue-shifted multiphoton-like resonances in a tunneling-dominated absorption channel near the Keldysh crossover.
sections.claimed_result: The authors interpret the blue-shifted resonances observed while varying drive field and frequency as a spectroscopic signature of adiabaticity breakdown in the Keldysh crossover.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; time-resolved optical spectroscopy on NiPS₃, compared with time-dependent Gaussian-variational Hubbard-model simulations
sections.unique_caveat: The interpretation is supported by qualitative rather than quantitative agreement with the model simulations, and the abstract reports one correlated-insulator system.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.50 from 2 cross-lists (weighted component 0.50). The experimental spectroscopy plus a qualitative Hubbard-model comparison provide a concrete result among candidates at this score; no external-attention component is recorded.

sections.title: Observation of collective flatbands in hybrid Mie-grating THz metasurfaces
sections.abstract: Terahertz near-field measurements on free-standing hybrid Mie-resonator/grating metasurfaces reveal quasi-flat magnetic-dipolar bands and long-lived coherent oscillations.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report experimentally observed quasi-flat bands and show that changing grating width tunes resonances and raises Q while retaining quasi-flat dispersion; the Purcell enhancement is calculated.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; terahertz near-field measurements and spatial mapping, supplemented by Bloch-resolved Purcell calculations
sections.unique_caveat: The emitter/Purcell response is calculated rather than demonstrated with an emitter, and the reported metasurface behavior does not by itself establish a device-level application.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.50 from 2 cross-lists (weighted component 0.50). The paper pairs experimental band mapping with a concrete geometry-tuning result; no external-attention component is recorded.

sections.title: State-selective dynamical freezing in driven Rydberg atom chains
sections.abstract: Floquet perturbation theory explains how interaction-dependent spin-flip amplitudes determine which initial states in driven Rydberg chains exhibit dynamical freezing.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find that a many-body state freezes only when all available spin-flip interference amplitudes vanish, and identify spacing bounds outside which the benefit of two-frequency driving is lost.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; Floquet perturbation theory for periodically driven interacting Rydberg chains
sections.unique_caveat: The conclusions are tied to the model and driving regimes where the perturbative description is controlled; no experimental demonstration is reported in the abstract.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.50 from 2 cross-lists (weighted component 0.50), linking quantum physics and statistical/strongly correlated matter. The ranking reflects cross-listing only; no external-attention component is recorded.

sections.title: Revealing Dark Matter in the Dark-Electron Rate of Xenon Detectors
sections.abstract: The authors propose using a much larger fraction of xenon detectors’ single-electron event rate in an annual-modulation search for sub-GeV dark matter and estimate the resulting sensitivity.
sections.claimed_result: Using measured dark-electron rates, the authors project that annual modulation could improve sensitivity for XENONnT, LZ, PandaX and future xenon detectors; this is a proposed analysis, not a dark-matter detection.
sections.evidence_type: forecast/proposal; sensitivity estimates based on measured single-electron rates from present and planned xenon experiments
sections.unique_caveat: The projected gain depends on successfully extracting an annual modulation from backgrounds in the raw single-electron rate; no new signal is reported.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.50 from 2 cross-lists (weighted component 0.50). The detector-data analysis proposal connects phenomenology and experiment; no external-attention component is recorded.
